challenges.name: poison-message-evidence
challenges.title: Poison Message & Growing Queue: read the evidence
challenges.description: Since 09:02 the grade-submissions queue has grown from 200 to 80,000 waiting submissions and no grade has been published. Six statements on one evidence pack - the queue dashboard (A), the worker logs (B), the queue config (C) and the message and grader details (D) - take you from reading the evidence to a hypothesis, past two wrong explanations, to the fix and how to verify it.

questions.question:
Evidence A - queue dashboard, grade-submissions (FIFO, one message group "grading"):
time    waiting   graded/min  oldest message age
09:00       200          598     3 s
09:05     1,535            0     3 min 07 s
09:30    12,660            0    28 min 16 s
10:00    26,010            0    58 min 02 s
10:15    autoscaler: grader-worker replicas 2 -> 6
10:30    39,360            0     1 h 28 min
11:00    52,710            0     1 h 58 min
12:02    80,300            0     3 h 00 min
submissions received: about 445 per minute all morning

Evidence B - worker logs (grader-worker, all replicas):
09:02:14.031 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 attempt=1 ERROR ParseError: Unexpected token '\u0000' in JSON at position 4096
09:02:14.033 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 requeued at head of group "grading", next attempt in 30s (attempts: 1 of unlimited)
09:02:44.040 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 attempt=2 ERROR ParseError: Unexpected token '\u0000' in JSON at position 4096
09:02:44.041 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 requeued at head of group "grading", next attempt in 30s (attempts: 2 of unlimited)
... the same two lines every 30 s ...
10:15:52.310 grader-worker-2d11 idle: message group "grading" is locked by an in-flight message
12:01:44.102 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 attempt=360 ERROR ParseError: Unexpected token '\u0000' in JSON at position 4096

Statement: "Since 09:02 no submission other than sub_8812 has been attempted: every attempt in the logs is for the same job id, and nothing has been graded since then."
questions.explanation: True. Every attempt line in B names job=sub_8812, with the attempt counter going from 1 to 360 at one attempt every 30 s (3 hours = 10,800 s / 30 s = 360), and A shows 0 graded per minute from 09:05 while the waiting count rises. The other replicas only log that the group is locked. Reading the evidence means noticing what is absent too: no other job id appears at all. The common mistake is to read "80,000 waiting" as "the workers are busy with 80,000 jobs" when they are stuck on one.

questions.question:
Evidence B - worker logs (grader-worker, all replicas):
09:02:14.031 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 attempt=1 ERROR ParseError: Unexpected token '\u0000' in JSON at position 4096
09:02:14.033 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 requeued at head of group "grading", next attempt in 30s (attempts: 1 of unlimited)

09:02:44.041 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 requeued at head of group "grading", next attempt in 30s (attempts: 2 of unlimited)
... the same two lines every 30 s ...
10:15:52.310 grader-worker-2d11 idle: message group "grading" is locked by an in-flight message
12:01:44.102 grader-worker-7c9f job=sub_8812 attempt=360 ERROR ParseError: Unexpected token '\u0000' in JSON at position 4096

Evidence C - queue and consumer config, as deployed:
queue: grade-submissions
type: fifo
messageGroupId: "grading"      # one group: results are published in submission order
consumer:
  concurrency: 1               # per message group
retry:
  attempts: 0                  # 0 = unlimited
  backoff: { type: fixed, delay: 30s }
  onFailure: requeue-head
deadLetterQueue: none
alerts: none on queue depth or message age

Statement: "sub_8812 fails, goes back to the head of the only message group, and with concurrency 1 and unlimited attempts nothing behind it can start, so the queue grows by the arrival rate."
questions.explanation: True. This hypothesis explains all of the evidence. C allows one in-flight message per group, puts every submission in one group, requeues a failure at the head and never gives up (attempts: 0). B shows the result: the same message every 30 s. A shows the consequence: waiting grows by about 445 per minute, exactly the arrival rate, and the oldest message age grows with the clock. One message that can never succeed (a poison message) plus unlimited retries plus strict ordering is head-of-line blocking. Remove any one of the three and the incident does not happen: the message would be parked, or would block only its own group, or would be retried a few times and given up.

Statement: "The step from 2 to 6 grader workers at 10:15 was too small: the queue keeps growing because 6 workers cannot keep up with 445 submissions a minute."
questions.explanation: False. A shows no change at all after 10:15: graded/min stays at 0 and waiting keeps growing by the same amount every half hour. B says why: grader-worker-2d11 is idle because the message group "grading" is locked by an in-flight message. With one group and concurrency 1 per group, only one message can be in flight at a time however many workers run, and that message is sub_8812. Before 09:02 two workers graded about 600 per minute, more than the arrival rate. The misconception is that a growing queue always means too little capacity; here the capacity is idle.

Evidence D - the message and the grader:
sub_8812: learner u_4471, lesson ts-generics, enqueued 09:01:58, body 9.8 MB
report.json: cut at 4,096 bytes and padded with NUL bytes (sandbox log writer, output over 4 MB)
time to fail one attempt: 38 ms
grader duration p50 before 09:02: 1.1 s; sandbox CPU since 09:02: 2%

Statement: "The grader became slow at 09:02: grading now takes longer than the time between arrivals, which is why the backlog builds up."
questions.explanation: False. D shows one attempt failing in 38 ms, the grader's p50 before the incident at 1.1 s and the sandbox CPU at 2% since 09:02: the grader is idle, not slow. A slow grader would show a lower graded/min, not zero, and a backlog growing by the difference between arrivals and completions; A shows zero completions and growth equal to the full arrival rate. The misconception is to blame throughput when the evidence says nothing is being completed at all.

questions.question:
Evidence C - queue and consumer config, as deployed:
queue: grade-submissions
type: fifo
messageGroupId: "grading"      # one group: results are published in submission order
consumer:
  concurrency: 1               # per message group
retry:
  attempts: 0                  # 0 = unlimited
  backoff: { type: fixed, delay: 30s }
  onFailure: requeue-head
deadLetterQueue: none
alerts: none on queue depth or message age

Proposed change:
retry:
  attempts: 0                  # 0 = unlimited
  backoff: { type: exponential, delay: 30s, max: 1h }
  onFailure: requeue-head

Statement: "This change fixes the incident: sub_8812 is retried less and less often, so the submissions behind it get graded."
questions.explanation: False. With onFailure: requeue-head in a FIFO group with concurrency 1, the message keeps its place at the head while it waits for the next attempt, and the group stays locked during the wait. A longer delay makes the block longer, not shorter, and attempts: 0 still means it never leaves. Backoff helps with failures that go away on their own (a timeout, a 503); a truncated report fails the same way on every attempt. The fix is a bounded number of attempts, then moving the message to a dead-letter queue with its last error, an alert on the dead-letter queue, and going on with the next message.

Planned verification on staging, after setting attempts: 3 and a dead-letter queue: replay sub_8812's body, then 1,000 normal submissions, and watch the queue.

Statement: "With the fix, sub_8812 should be in the dead-letter queue about 60 s after its first attempt, with its ParseError as the last error, the 1,000 submissions should all be graded in order after it, and the alert on dead-letter depth should fire."
questions.explanation: True. Three attempts 30 s apart take about 60 s (first attempt, +30 s, +60 s), then the message leaves the group with its evidence (attempts, last error, time) and the next message starts. Replaying the real poison payload is what makes this a verification of this incident and not a generic test: it proves the parser error is now bounded. The checks to read: the dead-letter entry, the processed order, the waiting count back near zero and the alert. The alert matters because a dead-letter queue nobody watches turns a loud outage into silent data loss.

challenges.name: poison-message-growing-queue
challenges.title: Poison Message & Growing Queue
challenges.description: Since 09:02 the CodeDev grade-submissions queue has grown from 200 to 80,000 waiting submissions. The logs show the same job failing with a parser error every 30 seconds and going back to the head of the queue; nothing behind it is graded. The queue is FIFO with concurrency 1: workOnce(worker, now) is called once per second and may only attempt the message at the head; while the head waits for its retry (notBefore > now) nothing behind it may start. Fix workOnce so it follows the team's new retry policy: at most 3 attempts per message in total, whatever the error; after a failed attempt that is not the 3rd, the message stays at the head and is retried 30 s later; when the 3rd attempt fails, the message leaves the queue and is added to the dead-letter list with its id, its attempt count, its last error message and the current second, and the next message can be attempted from the next second on. A message that succeeds on any attempt is graded normally. Input (one JSON object on stdin): { until, sampleEvery, messages: [{ id, at, body }] }; each second from 0 to until, messages arriving at that second join the tail, then workOnce runs once. Output (printed by the runner): the graded submissions in order as "id@second", the dead-letter list as "id after N attempts at T: error", the queue depth sampled every sampleEvery seconds, and the message left at the head. Do not change the grader or the test runner.
hints: The starter retries every failure, forever, at the head. What should happen differently on the 3rd failed attempt of the same message, and which list should it end up in?

Look at the catch block of workOnce and at MAX_ATTEMPTS. head.attempts already counts the attempt that just failed. Only one branch should keep the message at the head; the other must remove it from the queue so the next message becomes the head.

A similar case with a limit of 2 attempts and a 10 s delay: a message fails at second 4 (attempt 1) and at second 14 (attempt 2). Attempt 2 is the last one, so at second 14 the message is parked with "after 2 attempts at 14" and its error, and the message behind it is attempted at second 15.
